# Instructions

In word search puzzles you get a square of letters and have to find specific words in them.

For example:

```text
jefblpepre
camdcimgtc
oivokprjsm
pbwasqroua
rixilelhrs
wolcqlirpc
screeaumgr
alxhpburyi
jalaycalmp
clojurermt
```

There are several programming languages hidden in the above square.

Words can be hidden in all kinds of directions: left-to-right, right-to-left, vertical and diagonal.

Given a puzzle and a list of words return the location of the first and last letter of each word.


Do NOT modify the tests or the build files except as stated below. Do not create new files unless the specification requires them; Helper classes may go only in the solution's package."

## Summary

I implemented the solution entirely in `src/main/java/WordSearcher.java` (the `Pair` and `WordLocation` classes were already complete with proper value equality, so I left them untouched).

The approach:
- **`search(Set<String>, char[][])`** — builds a `Map<String, Optional<WordLocation>>` with one entry per requested word, so words that aren't found map to `Optional.empty()`.
- **`findWord`** — scans every cell in the grid and, from each cell, tries all 8 directions (left, right, up, down, and the four diagonals). The first successful match wins.
- **`tryMatch`** — walks the word character-by-character along a direction, failing fast if a letter mismatches or the walk leaves the grid (which also naturally prevents wrap-around and line-concatenation false positives). On a full match it returns a `WordLocation` with 1-based coordinates: start at `(col+1, row+1)`, end offset by `(dx, dy) × (word.length − 1)`.
